disposition_reason: Six-month field trial in a mature CCN51 plantation in Huánuco, Peru comparing AMF, Callisia repens, their combination and biochar at 1% and 2% against an untreated control, with bean Cd (micro-fermented, dried beans), EDTA-available and total soil Cd. Bean Cd per treatment is extracted as findings (control and AMF means printed; others from printed percentages or Figure 1A) and each treatment as a measured control.
disposition_locator: Abstract p.1; Methods p.4-5; Results p.5; Figure 1 p.6; Discussion pp.8-9

study.design: field trial (randomized complete block, 3 blocks, 6 treatments)
study.material_scope: cocoa beans from 3 pods per sampled tree, micro-fermented 7 days and oven-dried to 8% moisture; soil 0-30 cm
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Grown at Huamancoto (Pumahuasi), Daniel Alomía Robles district, Leoncio Prado province, Huánuco, Peru (9°12'25" S, 75°56'17" W, 671 m); not market samples
study.sampling_unit: central tree of a 5-tree experimental unit (36 m2); 90 trees in trial area; one sampled tree per treatment per block
study.method: Beans: digestion with HNO3 (65%) and 'HCl4 (98%)', atomic absorption spectrophotometry (INACAL-certified laboratory); soil total Cd EPA 3050B and ICP-OES; available Cd 0.05 M EDTA pH 7.0, atomic emission
study.basis: micro-fermented 7 days, oven-dried at 60 °C to 8% moisture (as dried; not converted to dry weight)
study.qa: Laboratory certified by INACAL; no CRM, recovery or LOD reported

controls.control: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) consortium from cocoa rhizosphere: 1 kg soil inoculum (1x10^5 spores/g) applied to fine roots within canopy projection, mature CCN51
controls.comparator: untreated control trees under the same conventional farmer management (mean bean Cd 0.94 mg/kg); RCBD, 3 blocks, 1 sampled tree per unit; outcome 6 months after establishment
controls.outcome: Bean Cd 0.94 -> 0.56 mg/kg (-40.43%, LSD letters a vs c); EDTA-available soil Cd ~0.28 (control, Figure 1B) -> 0.19 mg/kg; total soil Cd not changed (p = 0.19); transfer factor (bean/available) ~3.0 vs ~3.35 control (Figure 1D, not significant, both 'b'). Trade-off: extractable P < 7 mg/kg and lower SOM (significant vs control). Beans still above 0.6 mg/kg.
controls.locator: Methods p.4; Results p.5; Figure 1A-D p.6; Discussion pp.8-9

controls.control: Callisia repens cover planted from cuttings (10 kg fresh biomass per plant) from trunk base to canopy projection
controls.comparator: untreated control trees under the same conventional farmer management (mean bean Cd 0.94 mg/kg); RCBD, 3 blocks, 1 sampled tree per unit; outcome 6 months after establishment
controls.outcome: Bean Cd 0.94 -> ~0.65 mg/kg (-30.85%, letters a vs bc); available soil Cd 0.19 mg/kg vs ~0.28 control; total soil Cd unchanged. Cd uptake by C. repens itself was not measured.
controls.locator: Methods p.4; Results p.5; Figure 1A-D p.6; Discussion pp.8-9

controls.control: AMF inoculum plus Callisia repens combined (same doses as individual treatments)
controls.comparator: untreated control trees under the same conventional farmer management (mean bean Cd 0.94 mg/kg); RCBD, 3 blocks, 1 sampled tree per unit; outcome 6 months after establishment
controls.outcome: Bean Cd 0.94 -> ~0.71 mg/kg (-24.47% per text; Figure 1A letters 'ac' do not separate it from control 'a'); available soil Cd 0.21 mg/kg vs ~0.28 control. Authors suggest a negative interaction between AMF and C. repens.
controls.locator: Methods p.4; Results p.5; Figure 1A-D p.6; Discussion pp.8-9

controls.control: Biochar from maize residues and pine pruning (rotary pyrolysis 500 °C, 2 h; OM 82.12%, ash 17.88%, C 26.28%) at 1% w/w (8 kg per plant) spread over canopy projection
controls.comparator: untreated control trees under the same conventional farmer management (mean bean Cd 0.94 mg/kg); RCBD, 3 blocks, 1 sampled tree per unit; outcome 6 months after establishment
controls.outcome: Bean Cd 0.94 -> ~0.81 mg/kg (graph read; not significant, letters a vs ac); available soil Cd ~0.255 mg/kg (graph read, 'ab', not significant); SOM rose to 3.72% and extractable P above 10 mg/kg; transfer factor not different.
controls.locator: Methods p.4; Results p.5; Figure 1A-D p.6; Discussion pp.8-9

controls.control: Same biochar at 2% w/w (16 kg per plant; about 46 t/ha organic matter)
controls.comparator: untreated control trees under the same conventional farmer management (mean bean Cd 0.94 mg/kg); RCBD, 3 blocks, 1 sampled tree per unit; outcome 6 months after establishment
controls.outcome: Bean Cd 0.94 -> ~0.875 mg/kg (graph read; not significant, letters a vs ab); available soil Cd 0.19 mg/kg (text says 19% below control; Figure 1B control ~0.28 implies ~32%); transfer factor rose to ~4.6 (significant, 'a' vs control 'b'); SOM 3.92%; extractable P above 10 mg/kg. Lower available Cd did not translate into lower bean Cd within 6 months.
controls.locator: Methods p.4; Results p.5; Figure 1A-D p.6; Discussion pp.8-9

context_notes: Site description cites prior (Villanueva 2019) values of 0.78 mg/kg total soil Cd and 1.07 mg/kg bean Cd; these are not measurements from this trial's plots. The trial's own mean soil values were 0.570 mg/kg total and 0.258 mg/kg EDTA-available Cd.
Soil pH 6.98-7.39, not different among treatments (p = 0.86); texture unchanged.
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary gives control/baseline bean Cd 1.07 mg/kg; the trial control mean is 0.94 mg/kg (1.07 is a cited 2019 site value).
Stored summary gives C. repens 0.74 mg/kg and AMF + C. repens 0.81 mg/kg; the printed percentages applied to the 0.94 control give 0.65 and 0.71 mg/kg, matching Figure 1A.

Stored summary says bean Cd was quantified by ICP-OES after HNO3/HClO4 digestion; the primary says atomic absorption spectrophotometry after HNO3 and 'HCl4' digestion (ICP-OES was used for total soil Cd).
Stored summary implies each treatment reduction was p < 0.01; the primary gives one ANOVA p-value, and Figure 1A letters show the combined treatment not separated from control.
Stored summary states sample_n 90; 90 is the trees in the trial area, while one central tree per experimental unit was sampled (18 sampled trees, n=3 per treatment).
Stored summary cites the EU limit as 0.8 mg/kg for chocolate with >=50% cocoa solids; the primary only cites an EU range of 0.1-0.8 mg/kg for cocoa products, which apply to products, not beans.
integrity_issues: Discussion says 2% biochar reduced available Cd by 19% versus control, but Figure 1B shows control ~0.28 mg/kg vs 0.19 mg/kg (~32%) and the Results give 0.19 mg/kg.
Results cite 'Figure 1B' for the treatment effect on bean Cd; Figure 1B is available soil Cd (bean Cd is Figure 1A).
Combined AMF + C. repens is reported as a significant 24.47% reduction, but its LSD letters ('ac') overlap with the control ('a').
Digestion reagent 'HCl4 (98%)' is probably perchloric acid (HClO4); not verifiable from the text.
Authors compare bean Cd with EU limits for cocoa products (0.1-0.8 mg/kg); those limits do not apply to raw beans.
unresolved: Collection dates (calendar year/season) are not reported; only 'six months after treatment establishment'.

Means for C. repens and the combined treatment are calculated from printed percentages; biochar means, all medians and ranges are graph readings (about ±0.01 mg/kg) because no table of values is printed.
Whether the three pods per tree were composited into one sample is not stated explicitly; n=3 per treatment is inferred from the block design.
No LOD/LOQ, CRM or recovery is reported for bean Cd by AAS.
